messages.content: Explain how a hash table works in 3-4 sentences, using the analogy of a library catalog system.

A hash table works like a library catalog where each book (data) gets a unique call number (hash) that points directly to its shelf location (array index). When you want a book, you compute its call number and go straight to that shelf instead of searching every shelf. Collisions happen when two books get the same call number, handled by chaining (a small list at that shelf) or open addressing (checking the next shelf). This gives average O(1) lookup time, just as a good catalog lets you find any book in one trip.

judge_reason: The assistant explained how a hash table works in exactly 4 sentences and consistently used the requested analogy of a library catalog system.
